subsystems.name: Detector pixels
subsystems.role: convert a single photon into a measurable electrical pulse.
parts: superconducting nanowire meander (niobium nitride or tungsten silicide)
single-photon avalanche diode or silicon photomultiplier microcell

subsystems.name: Readout multiplexing
subsystems.role: route signals from thousands of pixels to a manageable number of output lines.

subsystems.name: Timing electronics
subsystems.role: record when each pixel fired, often to tens of picoseconds.

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: keep superconducting pixels below their critical temperature and reduce dark counts.

subsystems.name: Optical coupling
subsystems.role: deliver light efficiently to each pixel.

subsystems.name: Control and data system
subsystems.role: acquire, timestamp and correlate millions of events per second.

buildSteps.title: Design the array
buildSteps.detail: Choose pixel size, spacing, nanowire width or microcell geometry, and readout scheme for the target wavelength and count rate.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the detector wafer
buildSteps.detail: Deposit a thin superconducting film (for nanowire detectors) or build avalanche diodes in a silicon CMOS process.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the pixels
buildSteps.detail: Use electron-beam or deep-ultraviolet lithography to etch meandering nanowires or define microcells and their isolation trenches.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the readout
buildSteps.detail: Flip-chip or wire-bond the detector array to a cryogenic or CMOS multiplexing chip, forming electrical connections to every pixel.

buildSteps.title: Package and cool
buildSteps.detail: Mount the stack on a cold stage, align optical fibres or microlenses, and cool it to operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Characterise performance
buildSteps.detail: Measure detection efficiency, timing jitter, dark-count rate, afterpulsing and crosstalk across the array.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and scale
buildSteps.detail: Map each pixel’s position and timing offset, then extend to larger arrays while keeping yield and uniformity acceptable.

buildSteps.title: Deploy in a system
buildSteps.detail: Combine the array with lasers, optics and timing electronics for lidar, quantum communication or microscopy.

prerequisites.why: give the best timing jitter and low dark counts, but only at cryogenic temperatures.
offer room-temperature single-photon detection and large pixel counts for lidar and medical imaging.

pathway.milestone: kilopixel superconducting arrays and large silicon photomultiplier arrays in commercial instruments
pathway.unlocks: photon-starved imaging, fluorescence lifetime microscopy and automotive lidar.

pathway.milestone: megapixel-scale superconducting arrays with integrated cryogenic readout
pathway.unlocks: high-rate quantum communication receivers and long-range single-photon lidar.

pathway.milestone: photonic-integrated detector chips that combine waveguides, filters and arrays
pathway.unlocks: compact, alignment-free quantum and sensing systems.

pathway.milestone: wafer-scale single-photon imagers with per-pixel timing
pathway.unlocks: low-light cameras that count and time every photon across a wide field of view.
